approach: The ground is smooth, so only friction between the two blocks acts; the faster bottom block drags the top one forward while it itself slows down.

steps.text: The bottom (2 kg) block moves faster (8 m/s) than the top (1 kg) block (2 m/s), so kinetic friction from the 1 kg block acts backward on the 2 kg block and forward on the 1 kg block.
Find each block's acceleration. The 1 kg block feels only this forward friction; the 2 kg block feels only the equal, opposite friction (the ground beneath it is smooth).
Set the two velocities equal to find when they reach a common speed.
Find the common velocity at that time.
Find each block's displacement in that 1 s using s = v₀t + ½at².

final_answer.value: (a) t = 1 s, (b) common velocity = 6 m/s, (c) displacement of 1 kg block = 4 m, displacement of 2 kg block = 7 m

common_mistakes.text: Applying friction to the 2 kg block from the ground as well, even though the ground is stated to be smooth, which changes its acceleration and the final time.
Swapping which block speeds up and which slows down, giving friction the wrong direction on each block.
